$description: The Media workspace's library (`specs/studio.md` §22.6): the project's media as filters, a grid and the selected file's detail. ONE document in two modes. In `manage` it is the Media home tab, with Replace, Open in viewer and Delete under the detail; in `pick` it is the full-size picker inside a `jx-dialog` (`media-pick-dialog.json`), and the dialog's own footer answers Cancel or Use <file>. `media/media-library.ts` keeps every decision (which files a filter keeps, the sort, what a count may claim, where an arrow lands, what Replace writes) and hands this document strings and discriminants. **Unused is drawn with no number until the usage sweep has settled**, and Missing alt text and tags are not drawn at all: each needs a store that does not exist, and a filter that cannot be answered is not shipped as one that always answers nothing.

style.$description: Three columns over the whole stage: the filters, the grid with its toolbar, and the selected file's detail. Fills the pane's stage by its own geometry, as the workspace home does: the stage is `position: relative` (`pane-grid.json`). In pick mode the same columns fill the dialog's body instead, so the root's box is the only thing that differs between the two modes.

&[data-mode=\"pick\"].$description: Inside a dialog there is no stage to fill: the box is the dialog body's, at a height the dialog can scroll within.

&[data-drop=\"true\"].$description: The drop affordance is a STATE the flow holds, not a class a handler adds and forgets to take off.

& [part=\"upload\"], & [part=\"empty-upl.$description: A LABEL around the file picker, not a button that clicks a hidden one: the picker is the control, so it takes focus, Enter opens it and a screen reader announces a file upload. A plain element because a label forwards a click to the input it contains and a custom element between the two would break that.

& [part=\"upload-input\"], & [part=\"rep.$description: Out of the way but still FOCUSABLE: `display: none` would take the control out of the tab order, and the label around it draws the focus ring for it.

& [part=\"grid\"].$description: auto-fill over a minimum tile width; `media/media-library-model.ts` `gridColumns` does the same arithmetic, so ArrowDown lands on the tile drawn under the current one. Keep the two numbers in step.

& [part=\"preview-specimen\"].$description: The viewer's specimen at a side pane's size. The face arrives as the `@font-face` the flow writes under a family name generated from the path (`media/media-pane.ts` `specimenOf`); the element carries only that name, as a custom property, and the fallback stack is a rule, here.

ondragover.description: A file dropped ANYWHERE on the library uploads, to the destination the Upload label names before the drop: public/media/.

onchange.description: The picker itself, so the destination in the label's tooltip is visible BEFORE the files are chosen. The flow takes the element rather than the file list because a file input that is not cleared refuses the same file twice.

onkeydown.description: The grid pattern: arrows move one tile, Home and End to the ends of the row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the ends of the grid, and Enter opens the selected file (in pick mode, uses it). The flow computes where the move lands; the tile that receives it takes focus, so the roving tabindex follows the selection.

onfocus.description: Selection follows focus, the listbox pattern: a Tab onto the grid lands on the roving stop and selects it, so the first Enter opens (in pick mode, uses) the tile the focus ring is on rather than nothing.

children.$description: The thumbnail is asked for when the tile scrolls into view, not when the grid is built: `pending` until the flow's observer reports the tile, then the picture. A file the browser draws no picture of shows its kind's glyph.
Hidden on a host with no reference index, which is a different fact from "nothing uses it": a confident zero is the one answer this pane must never invent.

onchange.description: Replace writes the chosen file over this one's path, so every reference keeps resolving and now shows the new bytes (studio.md §9.3). The element rather than the list, so the input can be cleared.

children.$description: Manage mode's actions. Pick mode has none here: its answer is the dialog's own footer, Cancel and Use <file>.
